slides.title: T-Rex: Tactile-Reactive Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a variable-rate Mixture-of-Transformers architecture and a 100-hour tactile-rich dataset to improve robotic dexterity in tasks requiring delicate force control.

card.one_liner: T-Rex enables tactile-reactive dexterous manipulation using a variable-rate Mixture-of-Transformer architecture and a new 100-hour dataset.
card.key_idea: A Mixture-of-Transformer (MoT) framework that decouples low-frequency visuomotor planning from high-frequency tactile refinement using a spatio-temporal VQ-VAE encoder and cascaded flow matching.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 12 real-world contact-rich tasks; T-Rex achieved a 65% average success rate, outperforming the strongest baseline by over 30%.
card.limitation: Bottlenecked by hardware issues like sensor distortion, calibration drift, and a lack of dense palm sensing for whole-hand manipulation.

slides.title: HT-Bench: Benchmarking and Learning Dexterous Full-Hand Tactile Representations with Egocentric Vision
slides.highlight: This work introduces HT-Bench and HandTouch to align tactile observations with egocentric vision, supporting the MOSAIC goal of integrating ego-exo views and physics-based sensing for skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: HT-Bench is a large-scale benchmark for dexterous full-hand tactile representation learning using egocentric vision.
card.key_idea: HandTouch, a vector-quantized encoder, learns representations via a progressive three-stage pipeline: unimodal tactile reconstruction, cross-modal masked inpainting, and multimodal temporal frame prediction.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 10M RGB and 7.8M tactile frames across four tasks. HandTouch outperformed ResNet-18 and ViT baselines in retrieval, inpainting, and synthesis.
card.limitation: Focuses only on egocentric vision/full-hand tactile pairs; does not measure downstream robotic performance or cover other sensor types.

slides.title: Generating Natural and Expressive Robot Gestures through Iterative Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback using LLMs
slides.highlight: This research utilizes ChatGPT and reinforcement learning with human feedback to create more fluid and expressive co-speech gestures for the Pepper humanoid robot, advancing human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Iterative RLHF improves the expressiveness, relevance, and fluidity of LLM-generated co-speech gestures for humanoid robots.
card.key_idea: GPT-4 generates motion code from a primitive function library, refined through five iterations of offline DPO finetuning and online few-shot prompting based on human ratings.
card.evaluation: 250 participants rated 20 videos per iteration across 50 phrases. Results showed statistically significant improvements (p<0.001) in expressiveness, relevance, and fluidity by iteration 5.
card.limitation: Reliance on low-level primitives leads to repetitive patterns, mode collapse without history, and challenges in sustaining gesture diversity.

slides.title: MuseVLA: An Adaptive Multimodal Sensing Vision-Language-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation
slides.highlight: MuseVLA integrates diverse sensing modalities like temperature, sound, and radar into a VLA model for robotic manipulation. This supports HyECHO's focus on non-data-hungry multimodal perception for understanding complex states.

card.one_liner: MuseVLA adaptively selects non-visual sensors as on-demand tools to improve robotic manipulation of physical properties.
card.key_idea: Uses learnable sensor tokens for adaptive modality selection and "grounded sensor images" to unify heterogeneous sensor data into RGB space for a shared VLM backbone.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on real-world dexterous hand tasks (thermal, audio, radar) against RGB-only and raw-sensor baselines; achieved 80.6% average success rate.
card.limitation: Depends on a performant external segmentation module and is limited by a modest scale of real-world datasets.

slides.title: ROVE: Unlocking Human Interventions for Humanoid Manipulation via Reinforcement Learning
slides.tldr: RL FRAMEWORK FOR HUMANOID MANIPULATION WITH IMPERFECT INTERVENTIONS
slides.highlight: ROVE introduces a reinforcement learning framework that utilizes imperfect human interventions and cross-embodiment videos to improve humanoid manipulation. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: ROVE improves humanoid VLA policies by learning from imperfect human interventions using optimistic value estimation.
card.key_idea: A RL framework using Optimistic Value Estimation (OVE) and cross-embodiment human videos to extract high-value recovery behaviors from suboptimal, mixed-quality humanoid teleoperation trajectories.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on two real-world humanoid tasks (whiteboard erasing, toaster bread placement) against SFT and experience-learning baselines; showed consistent iterative improvement.
card.limitation: Lacks end-effector sensing (wrist cameras/tactile feedback), does not yet handle loco-manipulation, and is primarily an offline/iterative offline RL framework.

slides.title: Belt-Finger: An Affordable Soft Belt-Driven Gripper for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
slides.tldr: SOFT BELT-DRIVEN GRIPPER FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a soft belt-driven gripper that adds translation, pitch, and roll degrees of freedom, supporting the dexterous manipulation and skill acquisition goals of MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: An affordable, 3D-printable parallel-gripper upgrade adding translation, pitch, and roll for dexterous in-hand manipulation.
card.key_idea: A soft TPU-belt-driven finger module integrated with a stochastic iCEM-based MPC and a teleoperation interface for precise object control.
card.evaluation: Tested via teleoperation, MPC, and VLA fine-tuning on daily tasks; outperformed parallel grippers in success rates and efficiency.
card.limitation: Limited pitch for small objects, nonlinear rotations due to friction/wear, and precision loss from TPU belt elasticity.

slides.title: FlowMaps: Modeling Long-Term Multimodal Object Dynamics with Flow Matching
slides.highlight: FlowMaps uses latent flow matching to predict multimodal distributions of object locations based on human interaction patterns, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of environment states.

card.one_liner: FlowMaps predicts multimodal future 3D object locations in dynamic environments using latent flow matching.
card.key_idea: A VAE encodes object geometry/semantics, while a Conditional Diffusion Transformer (CDiT) learns a flow to predict future 3D bounding boxes conditioned on scene context.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 600+ ProcTHOR episodes and real-world TIAGo robot; outperformed baselines in Success Rate (SR) and Success weighted by Path Length (SPL).
card.limitation: Limited to a closed set of 41 object classes and 17 receptacles; requires large-scale training data.

slides.title: Tri-Info: Generalizable, Interpretable Failure Prediction for VLA Models via Information Theory
slides.highlight: Tri-Info uses information-theoretic signals to detect VLA model failures, offering strong cross-domain generalization and interpretable diagnostics without retraining.

card.one_liner: Tri-Info uses information-theoretic signals to provide generalizable and interpretable failure prediction for VLA models.
card.key_idea: It derives three complementary signals—action entropy, temporal consistency, and action-state coupling—processed via GRUs to detect failures across different architectures and environments without retraining.
card.evaluation: Tested on six VLA models across LIBERO, CALVIN, and ALOHA. Achieved 83% accuracy on real-world sim-to-real transfer where embedding-based baselines collapsed.
card.limitation: The method provides failure diagnostics and alarms but does not yet implement automated recovery actions.
